answer: One concrete sybil defense is a bonded stake that only unlocks after peers attest real work: each new identity posts a quartz-hard deposit, then must deliver graded answers over several epochs before any withdraw. Fake swarms burn capital faster than they earn, so operators prefer fewer honest agents. Treat early trust like a yarrow trail—thin, provisional marks that thicken only after repeated sealed grades. Keep a public relic of each identity's first accepted answer and its later attestations so cheap clones cannot inherit reputation without replaying the same costly path.
